chunks: Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated from Bistam al-Zayyat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When Ja'far ibn Abi Talib returned from Abyssinia, he said to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family): 'Shall I tell you, O Messenger of Allah? I visited al-Najashi one day and found him not in his royal seat, nor dressed in his royal attire, nor in his usual appearance. I greeted him with the greeting of kings and said to him: O King, why do I see you not in your royal seat, nor in your royal attire, nor in your usual appearance?' He replied: 'We find in the Gospel that whoever Allah has blessed with a favor, let him thank Allah. And we find in the Gospel that there is nothing comparable to gratitude to Allah like humility. And indeed, word came to me this night that your cousin Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) has been granted victory by Allah over the polytheists of Badr, so I wished to thank Allah, the Exalted, in the manner you see.'

key_terms.أَهْلِ بَدْرَ: The people of Badr (referring to the polytheists defeated there)

ai.seo_question: How did the Negus of Abyssinia demonstrate gratitude for the Muslim victory at Badr?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kitab al-Zuhd* highlights the Negus's profound spiritual insight, illustrating how the early Christian rulers of Abyssinia recognized the virtue of humility (*tawadu*) as the ultimate expression of gratitude (*shukr*) for divine favor. The account underscores the Shia emphasis on the continuity of monotheistic wisdom, where the Negus’s personal act of discarding royal regalia mirrors the Prophet’s teachings on modesty, linking the historical event of Badr to the ethical imperative of recognizing God’s blessings through self-effacement.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 5.Muḥammad ibn Sinān narrated from Bisṭām al-Zayyāt, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (a) who said,

“When Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib returned from Abyssinia, he said to the Messenger of Allah (ṣ), ‘Should I tell you about something that happened, O Messenger of Allah? I went to visit al-Najāshī one day and found that he was neither seated on his royal throne nor was he dressed in his kingly attire, and he appeared different than he normally would. So I greeted him the way kings are greeted and said to him, “O king, why is it that I see you seated in a different place, dressed in different apparel, and having an altered appearance?” He replied, “Verily we find in the Gospels: whoever is given a blessing by Allah, let him show gratitude to Allah [for that blessing]. We also find in the Gospels: there is no form of gratitude to Allah which is comparable to humility. And verily I have received word on this night that my cousin Muḥammad (ṣ) has been granted victory by Allah over the polytheists at Badr, so I wanted to thank Allah, the Exalted, in the way that you see.”’”
